items.text: Understand the difference between static and dynamic websites
Know why S3 is preferred over EC2 for static website hosting
Understand that making an S3 bucket public requires two steps: disabling Block Public Access AND adding a bucket policy
Understand what a CDN is and how it reduces latency using edge locations
Know what Amazon CloudFront is and what a distribution means
Understand OAC (Origin Access Control) and why it keeps S3 buckets private
Know the difference between edge locations, Availability Zones, and Regions
Understand TTL, cache hits, and cache misses
Enable S3 Static Website Hosting and set index/error documents
Write a bucket policy to grant public s3:GetObject access
Create a CloudFront distribution with S3 bucket as origin
Enable OAC and apply the auto-generated bucket policy to S3
Set the Default Root Object in a CloudFront distribution
Verify the setup: CloudFront URL works, direct S3 URL gives 403
Can explain the two-step public access process for S3
Can identify when to use CloudFront vs just S3 hosting
Can explain OAC and write the structure of an OAC bucket policy
Can describe what happens on cache hit vs cache miss
Know that CloudFront works with S3, ALB, EC2, and API Gateway — not just S3
Know that OAC replaced OAI and why OAC is better
